The "Belgrave" Cup was retained by Ray Hall, rather unfit after his Roman holiday, with John Morris gaining his first runners-up medal in a Club Championship.
Fred Denny and John Morris both retired in the first half of the race. Harry Shields " just out for a stroll" finally managed to beat second class standard by 5 secs. after 53 miles.
Although John Morris, Bernard Eglington, John Keown and Bob Farley fought hard to make up team places,this was to affect the team result considerably in the end.

We won the Team event with the very low score of 8 pts from S.W.C (21pts) and Woodford (30pts). John Morris walked a very strong race from halfway to finish 9th, and his performance augured well for the "Brighton" a month later.

Despite fine support from John Morris and Bernard Eglington we were obliged, however, to concede the team title to Surrey WC. The field included Gordon Hazle (Germiston Callies Harriers) the South African Champion, and Dennis Read (Steyning AC) the holder and brother of Norman Read the Rome Olympics gold medallist.
Our leading two were now placed 9th and 11th and with George Beecham and John Morris making progress down the field we were certainly in with a chance in the team race.
Our only entries in the Southern Counties AAA track '7' at Battersea Park on March 5th were Ray Middleton and John Morris.
John Morris caught George Beecham during the second half of the race and these two had a battle right up to the line when they were both given the same time.
John Morris failed to beat second class standard by just 29 seconds. The hot sun took its toll leading to Tom Cook's retirement at 19 miles.
Those Belgrave landmarks John Keown, John Morris and George Beecham are still very much alive and will, one hopes shortly be joined by John Johnson.

The veterans of Belgrave, well versed in the ways of the Brighton road, stand quietly out of the way of brasher newcomers with less experience and more to say;John Keown and John Morris are joined this year by John Johnson and Wally Wortley.
Come the Barking-Southend, our first man home was John Morris, tenth in 5hrs. 42m. 35s., with Doug Fotheringham not far behind in 12th place (5hrs. 48m. 35s.).
On June 25/26 in an Open 100 Miles Walking Race promoted by Surrey W.C., three Belgravians, John Moullin, John Morris and John Keown became Centurions when they finished the distance inside 24 hours.
Lower down the field, stride for stride, came John Keown (473) and John Morris (474) finishing together in 20:49:27. They took second team prize and are still active, further anecdotes unnecessary!

Despite this, Bels proved their worth to finish 3rd with Ray Middleton leading us home closely followed by Carl Lawton. Then came John Dunsford and Dave King, and John Keown and John Morris closed in.
John Morris

John Keown has completed 17 successive Brightons, and of those in this year's race Dave King and John Morris have notched up 11. Dave King now has six winning team medals (between 1965-75) and is chasing George Beecham's seven winning team medals (1956-68).

Ron Day, Dave King, John Morris, John Keown and Bob Picton saw to it that Belgrave retained that London to Brighton trophy. Ron became Belgrave champion at his first attempt at this 54 mile race and did particularly well on his melons and accolade.
A little way down the road at about 15 miles Dave King and Ron Day were together and later on came John Morris, John Keown and Bob Picton, all going well.

About halfway John Morris retired; our remaining four were still going strong. Dave was able to open up a gap on Ron (suffering the effects of a recent cold) but Ron always had Dave in sight on the long stretches - it's always good to have someone in view on these long efforts!

These performances would not have been possible without help on the road by others so a tribute to the selfless efforts of Charlie McLennan, Jack Goswell, Bob Barnes, Gerry Cameron, Bob Picton, Carl Lawton and Pat Duncan, and when not competing against him, John Morris.

The Festival of Walking promoted by the Borough of Enfield H. drew a number of us to Enfield and amongst our participants we had three from each of the McDermot and Nicholls families with John Morris and son (Peter) as well.
One "regular" we missed was John Morris who was unfit. However, he didn't deny us for he soon came through the field on his motor-cycle, with Peter on the back, to help our pair along.

John Morris, Belgrave's stalwart long distance walker, showed that he is still a force to be reckoned with when in December he regained the Colnbrook long distance walk championship in 2 hours 21 minutes 34 seconds.

John Morris and John Keown did credit to themselves by completing the distance, John Morris with his fastest time to date, and John Keown fighting through a bad patch - 30 miles of it - in which lesser mortals would have called it a day.

He was followed by Derrick Ellis 10th, 5:39.22 and John Morris 22nd, 5:57.10. Also in the race were three cadets but they were not competing in the actual race, they were Mark Harrison, Charles Long and Russell Day who finished up as the winning cadets team.
Belgrave's team consisted of Ron Day and the 'terrible twins' Johnny Morris and John Keown. For Ron this was his first attempt at 100 miles.
John Keown, John Morris and Ron Day. Unfortunately although we started a team we could get no further as both Johns, stalwarts that they are, retired.

Other clubs then get men finishing and just before second-class standard time is up John Morris comes in. Yes, it's the same chap who is a Field Events Judge and does such a lot for us including committee work, he also trains Peter and Ros.
Also to George Beecham who in the Endeavour 24 hours at Brighton became the newest member of the Centurions and together with John Morris won the team award.

Congratulations to Ron Langheim and John Morris on being elected life members at this years A.G.M. Brian Pritchard was elected Vice President in recognition of his years of work with our younger members.
100 x 1 mile protagonists. Left New Life Member John Morris hands over to new Vice President Brian Pritchard. Right Bill Couzens hits the come-back trail.

Carl Lawton had acted as helper in the previous three but this time competed along with John Dunsford, Ron Day and John Morris. A pleasant evening start and a cool night followed with Ed Shillabeer taking a 20 minute lead by 30 miles and Carl 2nd.
John Morris, Fred Denny, Richard Dorman, JOE COLEMAN, John Llewellin,Ed. Crossingham, Tom Carter, Ted Stimpson, Kneeling; Graham Seatter, Ron Day, John Hall.
For yet another year Belgrave did not field a team in the Hastings to Brighton, John Dunsford was 18th 6:49.36; John Morris 20th 7.06.26.

Belgrave, however, had no wins or records, once again it was left to John Morris and John Keown to fly the colours, John Keown was only going for 100 kms and John, 'there's no way you can't finish a 24 hour' Morris retired hurt at 75 miles.
